channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: At least 1,300 people arrested in mass weekend protests across France
item.description: At least 1,300 people were arrested on the sidelines of Saturday's protests across France and at least 50 officers and three protesters were hurt, the interior ministry said Sunday. The arrests occurred as clashes broke out on the margins of largely calm demonstrations in major cities over the high cost of living.

item.title: 12 injured, including 6 children, in shooting near Florida university, police say
item.description: At least 11 of those injured had gunshot wounds, police said.

item.title: Suspect in racist gun attack near Paris transferred to psychiatric unit
item.description: A shooter suspected of killing one person and wounding five others on Friday in the town of Trappes, near Paris, has had his police custody suspended for a 48-hour psychiatric observation, anti-terror prosecutors said Sunday. The 39-year-old man is believed to have had racist motivations behind the gun attack as most of the victims had foreign origins.

item.title: When a teen posts a selfie, how much filter is 'too much' filter?
item.description: The recent Meta settlement includes a clause banning "cosmetic procedure filters" for teens. But defining what constitutes an extreme makeover isn't easy.

item.title: France: Some clashes erupted at end of protests
item.description: There were some clashes on Saturday, mainly in major cities and as demonstrations came to an end. French authorities say police made nearly 1,000 arrests nationwide. Here’s a report from our sister channel, France 2.

item.title: More than 400.000 protest across France
item.description: Saturday’s demonstrations across France were largely peaceful, easing fears of a repeat of the violence seen last weekend. Hundreds of thousands took to the streets to demand action on the rising cost of living and more funding for public services, with students, workers and retirees marching side by side. Many say their anger shows no sign of fading. The government put turnout at 410,000 nationwide, while the CGT union estimated the figure was almost twice as high. Here’s Jack Pownall with more.

item.title: France’s far right gathers as Le Pen prepares her presidential campaign
item.description: Meanwhile, France’s far-right National Rally is holding the second day of its party congress in Orléans, south of Paris. Marine Le Pen is expected to officially launch her presidential campaign in a speech later this afternoon, while Jordan Bardella is being re-elected as party leader. On Saturday, a large counter-demonstration against the far right was held in the city. For more on what’s happening there, let’s cross to our reporter, Antonia Kerrigan.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands march in France to protest against government
item.description: Hundreds of thousands marched across France on Saturday protesting the rising cost of living and a lack of government resources for essential services like schools. While demonstrations in Paris started peacefully they ended with a heavy security response, with almost 1,000 arrested across the country. France 24 International Affairs Editor Oliver Farry shares further details.

item.title: More dads taking paid family leave for a new baby, sometimes as much as moms are
item.description: The U.S. has no national law for paid parental leave. But in states that do, more dads are using the benefit, sometimes more than moms. The change comes as Americans say having kids is unaffordable.

item.title: In Arkansas, Democrats see an opening at the edge of the competitive midterms map
item.description: In a sign of the potentially dire midterm political environment, Republicans have spent millions of dollars playing defense in Arkansas, one of the most conservative states in the country.

item.title: Independent candidates sense a moment in the West. Democrats are hoping they're right
item.description: As they look to win the Senate, Democrats are hoping that independent candidates in Nebraska and Montana can help them topple Republicans in a part of the country where their own brand is hurting.

item.title: Student protesters aim for electoral victory over Serbia's long serving leader
item.description: People in Serbia are voting in a parliamentary election that is being viewed as a showdown between former president Aleksandar Vucic and a university student protest movement.

item.title: Soldiers guard center of Milan as thousands of protesters march in cities across Europe
item.description: While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities Saturday from Milan to Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.

item.title: Serbia holds parliamentary election as populist leader Vucic faces student movement
item.description: Serbia votes on Sunday in what is set to be its most contested parliamentary election in more than 14 years, as a student-led movement seeks to oust the party of populist leader Aleksandar Vucic. The vote comes after nearly two years of student-led protests sparked by the 2024 collapse of a canopy that killed 16 people.

item.title: What to know as Brazilians choose between Lula and Bolsonaro in tense presidential runoff
item.description: Brazilians are set on Sunday to choose between leftist incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro in the runoff vote of a deeply polarizing presidential election, and one which will determine whether the US significantly expands its growing influence in Latin America.

item.title: PM open to 'honest discussion' about return to EU free movement
item.description: Andy Burnham says that an "honest discussion" is needed about readopting the EU's free movement rules.

item.title: Drought, fire and high diesel prices 'addin' up tough' for Oregon ranchers
item.description: Record diesel prices are kicking Western ranchers while they're down. Drought means they have to buy extra hay, and pay truckers extra to deliver it because of fuel price hikes.

item.title: Cornell student named in Jane Doe's civil suit seeks to be dropped from case
item.description: One of the Cornell students who was named in a civil lawsuit by a former undergraduate student known as Jane Doe, has asked a judge to drop him from the suit.

item.title: Amy Acton says Trump, Vance should 'look at the facts' after Ramaswamy attack ad
item.description: Ohio Democratic Amy Acton spoke to ABC News after a rally in Cleveland with former President Barack Obama.

item.title: Labour unveils £285m funding boost to 'shift power' to local leaders
item.description: Andy Burnham has announced £285m to fund local communities, declaring mayors shouldn't have to go "cap in hand to Westminster".

item.title: Brazilians go to polls today with left-winger and son of Trump ally neck and neck
item.description: Brazilians go to the polls on Sunday to elect a president in a run-off vote that is being closely watched around the world.

item.title: Archdiocese of New York agrees to $800 million settlement over sexual abuse claims
item.description: The 1,300 survivors of sexual abuse by clergy members and lay workers have all agreed to the settlement, according to an attorney for some of the plaintiffs.

item.title: Early voting begins in New York: What to know and the key races to watch
item.description: Saturday is the first day of early voting in New York and Empire State voters could help decide which party will control the House over the next two years.

item.description: Hundreds of thousands marched across France on Saturday protesting the rising cost of living and a lack of government resources for essential services like schools. While demonstrations in Paris started peacefully they ended with a heavy security response, with almost 1,000 arrested across the country.

item.title: Police to allow some offenders to breach curfews without arrest
item.description: The Metropolitan Police is reducing enforcement of offenders who breach their tag conditions amid resourcing pressures and following early prisoner release, Sky News understands.

item.title: WATCH: Obama, Trump hit the campaign trail ahead of critical midterm elections
item.description: Both the Democratic and Republican parties are now leaning into presidential power amid early voting for the midterm elections.

item.title: France: Watching the Post-Riot Protests
item.description: After the French protests turned into riots last weekend, the curfews, and then the alleged racist mass shooting yesterday on the outskirts of Paris, there has been much anxiety, planning and preparation ahead of today's protests.

item.title: “Witkoff should step down” says Ukraine Committee Chief
item.description: Ukraine’s access to Starlink and Starshield satellite links has been restored to the speeds it had before restrictions that disrupted front-line operations for more than a week, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday.

item.title: Thousands take to Tel Aviv's streets for protests against Netanyahu
item.description: Thousands marched against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government in Tel Aviv on Saturday – just three days before Israel's general election – demanding accountability for the failure to prevent a Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, which led to the war in Gaza.

item.title: Yemen's Houthi rebels claim new attacks on oil facilities and airports across Saudi Arabia
item.description: Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthi rebels said they launched attacks at Saudi oil facilities and airports on Saturday while Yemen’s Saudi-backed government ​said the ‌group also fired three ballistic missiles at coast guard sites in ⁠the port city of Aden.

item.title: France: Clashes erupt as protests sweep across cities
item.description: 🇫🇷 The Ministry of the Interior estimates at least 410,000 people rallied across France for Saturday’s protests against the high cost of living, including 110,000 in Paris. Meanwhile, reported nearly 800,000 demonstrators and 250,000 in the capital. The situation in Paris remained largely "calm" during the day, while clashes broke out in other cities following attempts to enter unauthorised areas.

item.title: Man charged with murder after body found in wheelie bin
item.description: A man has been charged with murder after a body was found in a wheelie bin.

item.title: Israel begins demolitions in West Bank
item.description: The Palestinian Authority has called for international pressure on Israel after a Palestinian official said around 1,200 Palestinians in Hebron in the West Bank were forced to leave their homes following an attack on Friday which killed two Israeli soldiers. The head of Hebron's municipality said an additional 1,300 may also be forced to leave.

item.title: Italy hit by new cost of living protests
item.description: Soldiers were deployed across Milan and luxury boutiques boarded up as protesters took to the streets again on Saturday, a week after looting and clashes with police. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced a series of measures, including sending an additional 500 soldiers to the city and introducing tougher penalties for minors, who police said made up a large proportion of last week’s violent protesters. Surveillance helicopters circled central Piazza del Duomo, while soldiers patrolled in groups alongside military vehicles and a water cannon. Some visitors said they would leave the city centre if violence broke out again. Our Rome correspondent, Seema Gupta, has the latest.

item.title: Paris: 70.000 police officers deployed nationwide
item.description: A coalition of the “Yellow Vests” movement, trade unions and students will march across France on Saturday with demands over studying conditions and purchasing power. Some 70,000 police are expected to be deployed as authorities fear looting and vandalism similar to last Saturday's unrest. Jennie Shin speaks to France 24's reporter Elitsa Gadeva.

item.title: France: Protests continue while police fire tear gas at demonstrators
item.description: A total of 410,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Saturday – including 110,000 in Paris – as part of a day of rallies focussed on purchasing power and the defence of public services, the Interior Ministry told AFP. The turnout was slightly lower than last week, which saw 550,000 people take to the streets. Meanwhile, according to the union responsible for organising the authorised events, 800,000 people participated in the demonstrations nationwide on Saturday, with 250,000 in the capital. Clashes broke out in several cities, including Paris, Lyon, Rennes, Nantes, Bordeaux, Nice, and Marseille. Matthew Mary-Caruchet shares further details.

item.title: WATCH: 2 brothers' Make-A-Wish visit to the Minnesota Vikings
item.description: The Yang brothers got to visit the Minnesota Vikings for Aiden's Make-A-Wish after his brother, Ryan, became his lifesaving bone marrow donor while battling leukemia.

item.title: WATCH: Halloween witches’ world record
item.description: A total of 184 people set a world record, decked out in pointed hats and witches’ cloaks, 400 feet up on the Orlando Eye.

item.title: NFL Paris Premier: The Saints' Alvin Kamara on global reach and sport as an opportunity for youth
item.description: FRANCE 24's François Picard and Selina Sykes are pleased to welcome New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara as the National Football League (NFL) expands its international reach to Paris. As the Saints prepare to face off with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Kamara calls the occasion as "an opportunity unlike any other" while reflecting on his remarkable career, his interest in representing his country in flag football at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, and his ambitions to develop sporting opportunities in Liberia, his parents' country of birth.

item.title: NFL's Paris Premier: Saints RB Alvin Kamara on global reach, sport as catalyst for youth opportunity
item.description: François Picard and Selina Sykes are pleased to welcome New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara. As the National Football League expands its international ambitions to Paris, FRANCE, Kamara offers a unique perspective that reaches well beyond the spectacle of American football's arrival in the French capital. Just days before the Saints' anticipated encounter with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Kamara describes the occasion as "an opportunity unlike any other," while reflecting on his remarkable career, his interest in representing his country in flag football at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, and his ambitions to develop sporting opportunities in Liberia, his parents' country of birth.

item.title: British and French paratroopers take part in major wargame in Germany
item.description: Over 2,500 British and French troops have taken part in a wargame in Germany designed to show how NATO territory could be defended against an attack.

item.title: Israel to close all West Bank land crossings on election day
item.description: Israel announced it would be closing all land crossings with the West Bank on the day of next week's parliamentary elections. The measure comes as Israel conducts a large-scale operation in the occupied Palestinian territory and 2,000 residents of Hebron have been displaced from their homes after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers in the area.

item.title: Israeli forces displace 2,000 Palestinians in Hebron after deadly attack on soldiers
item.description: The Palestinian Authority called for international pressure on Israel after a Palestinian official said around 1,200 Palestinians in Hebron in the West Bank were forced to leave their homes following an attack on Friday which killed two Israeli soldiers. Israeli defence minister Israel Katz later confirmed in an interview that the displacements had reached the 2,000 mark.

item.title: Starlink back to 'the level ⁠we need' in Ukraine, Zelenskyy says
item.description: The Starlink satellite system is back to operating at the speed Ukraine needs after slowing down for more than a week, damaging Kyiv's ability to defend itself from Russian attacks, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

item.title: Bahamas police investigate after British woman dies trying to rescue sons

item.description: The former ESPN reporter was appointed as a press adviser last month.

item.description: Dramatic video shows the rescue of two people stranded in the ocean after their boat sunk off the coast of Fort Myers, Florida. Both boaters are doing OK.

item.description: The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductee visited Griffiths Middle School in Downey, California, to surprise students at two local schools with new musical instruments.
